LESSON: PUTTING TOGETHER

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Numbers
Topic 2.7: Putting Together
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 10

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Putting Together, part of Numbers in SNE  /  physical-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: How many play objects are in each of the two small baskets? 2. How many play objects do you get after putting together play objects in two small baskets?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. Collect in purposive pairs/group different groups of similar play objects in school for counting carefully. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to collect play objects.

2. Observe in purposive pairs/group and talk about similar play objects within the school environment. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication (AAC) express their views.

3. Collaborate with others to put similar play objects together with a sum not exceeding nine and count. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. Collect in purposive pairs/group different groups of similar play objects in school for counting carefully. Learners with manipulative difficulties could use alternative functional parts of the body or assistive technology or be assisted by peers, learner support assistants or the teacher to collect play objects.
2. Observe in purposive pairs/group and talk about similar play objects within the school environment. Learners with speech difficulties could use Alternative and Augmentative modes of Communication (AAC) express their views.
3. Collaborate with others to put similar play objects together with a sum not exceeding nine and count. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Putting Together together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Collaboration and communication: learners work and talk with each other as they put together similar play objects with a sum

not exceeding 9 and count.

Values:
Respect: learners exercise patience while putting together play objects.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Safety: learners carefully collect similar play objects for counting from school environment.

Link to Other Activity Areas:

The learner is able to relate collecting similar play objects from the school environment to environmental cleanliness in

Environmental Activities.
